pr_title: Enabling additional vulkan extension and adding further checks
pr_body:
Slowly working my way through fixing #69951

_bugsquad edit:_ Fixes #69951
pr_comments:
Testing this out locally now. Running with the profile provided by Sakrel we get the following output:
```
ERROR: Your GPU doesn't support image cube arrays.
   at: (drivers\vulkan\vulkan_context.cpp:1287)
ERROR: Condition "err != OK" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_CREATE
   at: VulkanContext::_window_create (drivers\vulkan\vulkan_context.cpp:1631)
ERROR: Failed to create Vulkan Window.
   at: (platform\windows\display_server_windows.cpp:3638)
ERROR: Failed to create main window.
   at: (platform\windows\display_server_windows.cpp:3953)
Using "winink" pen tablet driver...

================================================================
CrashHandlerException: Program crashed
Engine version: Godot Engine v4.0.beta.custom_build (c513c0d39da954f448c740a5fdbad0da7d6f8adf)
Dumping the backtrace. Please include this when reporting the bug to the project developer.
[0] ???
[1] ???
[2] RendererCompositor::create (F:\dev\godot\servers\rendering\renderer_compositor.cpp:43)
[3] RenderingServerDefault::RenderingServerDefault (F:\dev\godot\servers\rendering\rendering_server_default.cpp:413)
[4] Main::setup2 (F:\dev\godot\main\main.cpp:2075)
[5] Main::setup (F:\dev\godot\main\main.cpp:1882)
[6] widechar_main (F:\dev\godot\platform\windows\godot_windows.cpp:164)
[7] _main (F:\dev\godot\platform\windows\godot_windows.cpp:203)
[8] main (F:\dev\godot\platform\windows\godot_windows.cpp:217)
[9] WinMain (F:\dev\godot\platform\windows\godot_windows.cpp:231)
[10] __scrt_common_main_seh (d:\a01\_work\6\s\src\vctools\crt\vcstartup\src\startup\exe_common.inl:288)
[11] <couldn't map PC to fn name>
-- END OF BACKTRACE --
================================================================
```

The initial error is good, but we should close the process safely instead of crashing. I'll enable for cubemap arrays and see what happens
After enabling support for imageCubeArrays, there is only one more validation error:
```
ERROR: VALIDATION - Message Id Number: -884533293 | Message Id Name: VUID-VkPipelineColorBlendStateCreateInfo-pAttachments-00605
        Validation Error: [ VUID-VkPipelineColorBlendStateCreateInfo-pAttachments-00605 ] Object 0: handle = 0x2457afa9380, type = VK_OBJECT_TYPE_DEVICE; | MessageID = 0xcb4717d3 | Invalid Pipeline CreateInfo[0]: If independent blend feature not enabled, all elements of pAttachments must be identical. The Vulkan spec states: If the independentBlend feature is not enabled, all elements of pAttachments must be identical (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.3.224.1/windows/1.3-extensions/vkspec.html#VUID-VkPipelineColorBlendStateCreateInfo-pAttachments-00605)
        Objects - 1
                Object[0] - VK_OBJECT_TYPE_DEVICE, Handle 2497439241088
   at: VulkanContext::_debug_messenger_callback (drivers\vulkan\vulkan_context.cpp:262)
```
I don't think this one was included in the OP, but we should fix it as well

> The initial error is good, but we should close the process safely instead of crashing. I'll enable for cubemap arrays and see what happens

That worries me a little, that means any error result from `_create_physical_device` would lead to a crash. I'll see how easy it is to fix that.

*edit*, ok so going down the call stack everything nicely returns errors due to this failure, until we get into the constructor of the relevant subclass of `RenderingDevice`. As we don't have a mechanism for exiting constructors with a failure it nicely hobbles on until we crash because we've not finished setting up the rendering pipeline.

I'm tempted to change `RenderingDevice` so the constructor does very little and instead it has an `init` or `setup` function that can return an error.

Looks like the profile provided in the issue is missing a bunch of device features. The updated profile is [here](https://gist.github.com/sakrel/a4f5a35ac65c4967d45c57fcbb73877c).
With the updated profile I get the following validation error when compiling the fsr shader:

> VUID-VkShaderModuleCreateInfo-pCode-01091(ERROR / SPEC): msgNum: -1480880714 - Validation Error: [ VUID-VkShaderModuleCreateInfo-pCode-01091 ] Object 0: handle = 0x1ea7b058460, type = VK_OBJECT_TYPE_DEVICE; | MessageID = 0xa7bb8db6 | vkCreateShaderModule(): The SPIR-V Capability (Int16) was declared, but none of the requirements were met to use it. The Vulkan spec states: If pCode declares any of the capabilities listed in the SPIR-V Environment appendix, one of the corresponding requirements must be satisfied (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.3.236.0/windows/1.3-extensions/vkspec.html#VUID-VkShaderModuleCreateInfo-pCode-01091)

I think to fix this validation error, this line must also check whether `VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures::shaderInt16` is supported: 
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1d14c054a12dacdc193b589e4afb0ef319ee2aae/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/effects/fsr.cpp#L45-L46
The `MODE_FSR_UPSCALE_NORMAL` define enables the `A_HALF` define which tells the fsr shader that both 16-bit integers and floats are supported.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1d14c054a12dacdc193b589e4afb0ef319ee2aae/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/effects/fsr_upscale.glsl#L40-L44
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1d14c054a12dacdc193b589e4afb0ef319ee2aae/thirdparty/amd-fsr/ffx_a.h#L57
@sakrel, I've added it to the check for `SUPPORTS_FSR_HALF_FLOAT` itself, it actually already checked various related things.

issue_context.title: Vulkan: Various validation errors related to device extensions and features
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

master

### System information

Windows 11, Vulkan, AMD Radeon RX 5700

### Issue description

1. Missing extension `VK_KHR_storage_buffer_storage_class` 
```
Missing extension required by the device extension VK_KHR_16bit_storage: VK_KHR_storage_buffer_storage_class. 
The Vulkan spec states: All required device extensions for each extension in the VkDeviceCreateInfo::ppEnabledExtensionNames list must also be present in that list (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.3.224.1/windows/1.3-extensions/vkspec.html#VUID-vkCreateDevice-ppEnabledExtensionNames-01387)
```
2. Missing extension `VK_KHR_maintenance2`
```
Missing extension required by the device extension VK_KHR_create_renderpass2: VK_KHR_maintenance2. 
The Vulkan spec states: All required device extensions for each extension in the VkDeviceCreateInfo::ppEnabledExtensionNames list must also be present in that list (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.3.224.1/windows/1.3-extensions/vkspec.html#VUID-vkCreateDevice-ppEnabledExtensionNames-01387)
```
```
Attempted to call vkCreateRenderPass2KHR() but its required extension VK_KHR_maintenance2 has not been enabled
```
4. `VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures::imageCubeArray` feature is not enabled. According to [vulkan.gpuinfo.org](https://vulkan.gpuinfo.org/listfeaturescore10.php?feature=imageCubeArray) `imageCubeArray` is supported by 98.44% of devices, so I think it should be fine to make this feature a requirement and fail initialization if this feature is not supported.
```
vkCreateImageView(): pCreateInfo->viewType can't be VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_CUBE_ARRAY without enabling the imageCubeArray feature. The Vulkan spec states: If the imageCubeArray feature is not enabled, viewType must not be VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_CUBE_ARRAY (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.3.224.1/windows/1.3-extensions/vkspec.html#VUID-VkImageViewCreateInfo-viewType-01004)
```
5. `VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures::samplerAnisotropy` feature is not enabled. `samplerAnisotropy` is supported by 90.12% of devices
```
vkCreateSampler(): Anisotropic sampling feature is not enabled, pCreateInfo->anisotropyEnable must be VK_FALSE. 
The Vulkan spec states: If the samplerAnisotropy feature is not enabled, anisotropyEnable must be VK_FALSE (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.3.224.1/windows/1.3-extensions/vkspec.html#VUID-VkSamplerCreateInfo-anisotropyEnable-01070)
```
6. `VkImageFormatListCreateInfoKHR` requires `VK_KHR_image_format_list` to be enabled
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_vulkan.cpp#L1663
```
vkCreateImage: Includes a pNext pointer (pCreateInfo->pNext) to a VkStructureType (VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_IMAGE_FORMAT_LIST_CREATE_INFO), but its parent extension VK_KHR_image_format_list has not been enabled. 
The Vulkan spec states: Each pNext member of any structure (including this one) in the pNext chain must be either NULL or a pointer to a valid instance of VkBufferCollectionImageCreateInfoFUCHSIA, VkDedicatedAllocationImageCreateInfoNV, VkExportMetalObjectCreateInfoEXT, VkExternalFormatANDROID, VkExternalMemoryImageCreateInfo, VkExternalMemoryImageCreateInfoNV, VkImageCompressionControlEXT, VkImageDrmFormatModifierExplicitCreateInfoEXT, VkImageDrmFormatModifierListCreateInfoEXT, VkImageFormatListCreateInfo, VkImageStencilUsageCreateInfo, VkImageSwapchainCreateInfoKHR, VkImportMetalIOSurfaceInfoEXT, VkImportMetalTextureInfoEXT, or VkVideoProfilesKHR (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.3.224.1/windows/1.3-extensions/vkspec.html#VUID-VkImageCreateInfo-pNext-pNext)
```
7. `VkImageViewUsageCreateInfo` requires `VK_KHR_maintenance2` to be enabled.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_vulkan.cpp#L2087-L2130
`RenderingDevice::texture_create_shared` currently assumes this extension is always enabled, so fixing this is probably a bit more involved than just enabling `VK_KHR_maintenance2` in `vulkan_context.cpp`
```
vkCreateImageView: Includes a pNext pointer (pCreateInfo->pNext) to a VkStructureType (VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_IMAGE_VIEW_USAGE_CREATE_INFO), but its parent extension VK_KHR_maintenance2 has not been enabled. 
The Vulkan spec states: Each pNext member of any structure (including this one) in the pNext chain must be either NULL or a pointer to a valid instance of VkExportMetalObjectCreateInfoEXT, VkImageViewASTCDecodeModeEXT, VkImageViewMinLodCreateInfoEXT, VkImageViewSampleWeightCreateInfoQCOM, VkImageViewUsageCreateInfo, or VkSamplerYcbcrConversionInfo (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.3.224.1/windows/1.3-extensions/vkspec.html#VUID-VkImageViewCreateInfo-pNext-pNext)
```

1. and 2. can be fixed by enabling the respective extension with `register_requested_device_extension` in `vulkan_context.cpp`


 


### Steps to reproduce

- Launch Vulkan Configurator
- Select the **Portability** Configuration
- Download [VP_SAKREL_vulkan_1_0_profile_with_device_features_disabled.json.txt](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10206849/VP_SAKREL_vulkan_1_0_profile_with_device_features_disabled.json.txt) and remove the `.txt` extension
- Select `VP_SAKREL_vulkan_1_0_profile_with_device_features_disabled.json` as profile
- Launch Godot



### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments: I'm not sure if we need [VK_KHR_maintenance2](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/man/html/VK_KHR_maintenance2.html), `vkCreateRenderPass2KHR` is enabled through [VK_KHR_create_renderpass2](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/man/html/VK_KHR_create_renderpass2.html) which we enable in device properties.

~~With using `TEXTURE_TYPE_CUBE_ARRAY` there isn't an extension we need to enable. Only reference I can find is that we need to add `VK_IMAGE_CREATE_CUBE_COMPATIBLE_BIT` to our create flags which we seem to do (unless there is a place where we forget).~~

Ah this is in specifying `pEnabledFeatures` in `VkDeviceCreateInfo`, we retrieve the structure with `vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures` to query what features are supported and re-use that when we create the device ensuring all supported features are enabled.

So we're going to start checking the feature flags for various features I guess and make a decision on which we require. I don't really see how we can live without cube arrays as they are central to our radiance map implementation and shadow maps for omni lights.

> So we're going to start checking the feature flags for various features I guess and make a decision on which we require. I don't really see how we can live without cube arrays as they are central to our radiance map implementation and shadow maps for omni lights.

Ya cube map arrays are absolutely required for us
Ok, so on #6, in the code we're already excluding the effected code on Android, we might be able to remove that and just check for the extension.

And #7 is also tricky, indeed we need to check for `VK_KHR_maintenance2` however `VkImageViewUsageCreateInfo` is not just relying on that, it is also a Vulkan 1.1 feature. We could make `VK_KHR_maintenance2` optional and only add this structure to `vkCreateImageView` if the extension is enabled but there may be further issues with not specifying this information.

review_comments: And we need to test this properly on a Vulkan 1.0 device, `VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_IMAGE_VIEW_USAGE_CREATE_INFO` is Vulkan 1.1 only and only available if the maintenance extension is supported.
Seems fine when emulating a Vulkan 1.0 device

One more to solve https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/70013

We are getting the crash because the device doesn't support using arrays of samplers, the Molten VK error comes from here:
https://github.com/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/blob/4fded82c679fcd8f743e9a86f46904ca9e85629c/MoltenVK/MoltenVK/GPUObjects/MVKDescriptor.mm#L647-L649

MoltenVK passes the presence of that feature using ``shaderSampledImageArrayNonUniformIndexing`` in the Vulkan Physical Device Features struct.

```suggestion
ERR_FAIL_COND_V_MSG(!physical_device_features.shaderSampledImageArrayNonUniformIndexing, ERR_CANT_CREATE, "Your GPU doesn't support shaderSampledImageArrayNonUniformIndexing which is required to use the Vulkan-based renderers in Godot.");

```

Hmm, should we be checking both individually then, or should it be a matter of only failing if both are not available?

I really need to start getting back into Mac, I have a Mac now to test but so used to working on Windows now :P
I don't think MoltenVK exposed any means for us to check them separately.

Ok this fails, it's actually not in `VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures`, it's in `VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features`. We'll need to add retrieving that data for our device (when possible) as well. This does mean that MoltenVK is guaranteed to support Vulkan 1.2?
Looking further into `VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features` it's a core function of Vulkan 1.2 and it actually replaces some of the others.

Ok I changed it around so we use `VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features` if available. There is probably more improvement possible here, I'm wondering for instance if we should cache the results better but thats for another day.

For now I've got the check for `shaderSampledImageArrayNonUniformIndexing` only applied when we do have Vulkan 1.2 support and only for MacOS. 
Not sure if we should do more for iOS and if we've not on Vulkan 1.2?

It should be for macOS and iOS as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/70013 was a report for iOS

But I think other than that our hands are tied as MoltenVK doesn't really give us anything better to my knowledge

_Edit: I spoke too soon, Doing a quick search through the MoltenVK github I see ``vkGetPhysicalDeviceMetalFeaturesMVK`` which has an ``arrayOfSamplers`` property_

We may need @bruvzg's help to see how we can call a MVK specific function
It should be tied into a vendor extension that we can check. Can't find anything on Google about it but if we find out if MoltenVK announces itself as an extension we could check that.

Checking the MoltenVK headers it identifies itself as a Vulkan 1.2.x implementation and they expose an extension `VK_MVK_MOLTENVK_EXTENSION_NAME` (`VK_MVK_moltenvk`) so we can probably check that.

I really need to take the time to setup my mac for testing
